findings.evidence: cmd = [sys.executable, str(REPO_ROOT / "scripts" / "agent_diff_check.py"), "--mod", "queue_hud_src", "--patch-out", ...]; res = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=str(REPO_ROOT), ...); self.assertEqual(res.returncode, 0, ...). In agent_diff_check.py, main passes --mod targets to run_build_checks (line 158), which runs scripts/build_check.py against the live working tree (lines 85-93).
findings.suggested_investigation: Run `python3 -I scripts/test_subagent_tools.py -k diff_check` on a clean tree and check how long it takes and whether build_check.py runs. Consider whether the test should use --no-patch and a fixture baseline, or mock run_build_checks, so it tests only the JSON output contract.
findings.why_it_matters: A unit test named test_diff_check_baseline_and_patch silently becomes a full build of queue_hud_src plus a baseline/test run against the live tree. Its result depends on build toolchain state and on uncommitted work in other files, so the test is slow and can fail for reasons unrelated to the diff checker logic. It also has no --no-patch or --baseline isolation.

findings.evidence: self.assertIn("verdict", data) / self.assertIn("changed_files", data) — the verdict value is never checked.
findings.suggested_investigation: Compare the verdict values that agent_diff_check.py --json can emit (see the verdict construction in agent_diff_check.py main, around lines 158-200) and assert the expected value for a clean tree versus a known violation.
findings.why_it_matters: The only verdict check is key presence, so a checker that always reports a non-PASS or always PASS verdict would still pass this test. The test does not exercise the gate outcome it is named after.
